claim_verdicts.evidence: collections.md l.40: "A List<T> stores elements in order and can grow or shrink as your program runs." List<T> remarks: "Elements in this collection can be accessed using an integer index. Indexes in this collection are zero-based."
List<T> remarks: "List<T> accepts null as a valid value for reference types and allows duplicate elements."

List<T>.Contains remarks: "This method performs a linear search; therefore, this method is an O(n) operation, where n is Count." collections.md l.53: O(n) "means the work grows roughly in proportion to the number of elements in the collection." The lesson makes no cost statement about positional access beyond "hands you a value by its position".

collections.md l.20: "A dictionary stores values that you reach by key instead of by position. Use Dictionary<TKey,TValue> when each element has a lookup key, such as a name, ID, or code." l.57: "A Dictionary<TKey,TValue> stores key/value pairs."

hashtable doc l.26: a search generates the hash code "and the bucket associated with that hash code is searched." Dictionary remarks: "the capacity is automatically increased as required by reallocating the internal array"; retrieval "close to O(1)". l.22 ties speed to the hash function: "a hash function that generates a unique hash code for each unique key results in better performance". Growth keeps groups short only when hash codes are spread out; the lesson says it unconditionally.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: It keeps more groups as it fills, so as long as different keys give different hash codes, each group stays a few values long and a lookup barely costs more as the dictionary grows.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Dictionary remarks: "For purposes of enumeration, each item in the dictionary is treated as a KeyValuePair<TKey,TValue> structure representing a value and its key. The order in which the items are returned is undefined."

Dictionary remarks: "As long as an object is used as a key in the Dictionary<TKey,TValue>, it must not change in any way that affects its hash value." Mechanism, hashtable doc l.26: an added object "is stored in the bucket that is associated with the hash code"; a search generates the hash code and "the bucket associated with that hash code is searched."

Dictionary remarks: "if you do not specify an implementation, the default generic equality comparer EqualityComparer<T>.Default is used." record.md l.118/128: compiler synthesizes Equals and "An override of Object.GetHashCode". Run (SDK 10.0.300): Dictionary keyed by a plain class, ContainsKey(new C(1)) -> False; keyed by a record, ContainsKey(new P(1,"a")) -> True.

TryGetValue signature "public bool TryGetValue(TKey key, out TValue value)"; returns "true if the Dictionary<TKey,TValue> contains an element with the specified key; otherwise, false"; remarks: "more efficient than catching the KeyNotFoundException thrown by the Item[] property." Run: byId[99] -> System.Collections.Generic.KeyNotFoundException.

ToDictionary<TSource,TKey>(source, keySelector) exceptions: "ArgumentException: keySelector produces duplicate keys for two elements." keySelector: "A function to extract a key from each element." Run: two elements with Id 1 -> System.ArgumentException.

HashSet<T> remarks: "A set is a collection that contains no duplicate elements". HashSet<T>.Add returns "false if the element is already present." Run: new HashSet<int>{2,3,2}.Count -> 2; sample prints "2 distinct ids, contains 3: True".

HashSet<T>.Contains remarks: "This method is an O(1) operation." HashSet<T> remarks: provides "high-performance set operations similar to accessing the keys of the Dictionary<TKey,TValue> or Hashtable collections."

Ran `dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- collections-choice` (SDK 10.0.300; CollectionsChoice.cs and its Program.cs entry identical to stage-0). Output: "1 Bàn phím cơ", "2 Chuột không dây", "3 Tai nghe", "product 2 is Chuột không dây", "2 distinct ids, contains 3: True".
collections.md l.20: "Choose the collection that matches how your code uses the data." The lesson states it as a rule tied to the question asked (outline item 2), not as a ranking.
Kind opinion; it restates the lesson situation (outline item 3) and follows from claims 3 and 17. No separate source needed.

List<T>.Contains and List<T>.Find remarks: "This method performs a linear search; therefore, this method is an O(n) operation, where n is Count." Repeating it once per outer element gives up to outer x n comparisons (20 x 50,000 = 1,000,000, arithmetic checked). TryGetValue: "This method approaches an O(1) operation."

List<T>.Find remarks: "The elements of the current List<T> are individually passed to the Predicate<T> delegate, moving forward in the List<T>, starting with the first element and ending with the last element. Processing is stopped when a match is found." and "This method performs a linear search".

issues.quote: It keeps more groups as it fills, so each group stays a few values long and a lookup barely costs more as it grows.
issues.text: Claim 5 rephrased: groups stay short only when keys spread over different hash codes. The docs tie lookup speed to the hash function ("a hash function that generates a unique hash code for each unique key results in better performance"); a key type whose GetHashCode returns few distinct values keeps long groups however many groups exist. The sentence states it unconditionally.
issues.fix: Replace with: "It keeps more groups as it fills, so as long as different keys give different hash codes, each group stays a few values long and a lookup barely costs more as the dictionary grows." Add the same condition to claim 5 in .meta.json.
